chemical-bond.def: An attraction that holds two or more atoms or ions together, caused by nuclei attracting electrons.

covalent-bond.def: A bond in which two atoms share a pair of electrons that both nuclei attract.

polar-covalent.def: A covalent bond in which the shared electrons are pulled closer to the more electronegative atom; if the atoms are identical the sharing is equal and the bond is nonpolar.

partial-charge.def: A charge smaller than one full electron charge, written δ+ or δ−, on the atoms of a polar bond.

dipole.def: A separation of positive and negative charge, such as the δ+ and δ− ends of a polar bond; drawn as an arrow pointing toward the negative end.

ionic-bond.def: The Coulombic attraction between oppositely charged ions, usually formed when a metal gives electrons to a nonmetal.

metallic-bond.def: The attraction between metal cations and the sea of delocalized valence electrons around them.

delocalization.def: Describes electrons that are not held between one pair of atoms but spread over several or many atoms, as in a metal.
